boundaries.origin: OpenAI native file-search session and matcher loop
intentional_changes: Replace a query-per-message backlog with latest-query coalescing and retained sticky walk/stop flags.
Separate the native session and matcher into focused modules; tagged query identity rejects stale completion and completed snapshots precede Idle.
boundaries.ownership: The existing native supervisor retains walker, matcher pool and reporter lifetime; queue wakeups do not transfer ownership.
limits: No installed backend selection or App Server/TUI composition is added by this module extraction.
Matching, score ordering and Unicode/highlight parity remain regression obligations.

boundaries.origin: Existing OpenAI walker/injection path with new explicit resource accounting
intentional_changes: Preflight fixed index/highlighting allocation and 2*T + 2 dedicated OS workers before native startup.
Atomically charge entry count and exact retained path/column bytes before allocating owned payloads; retain the first exhaustion and stop further admission.
Use a restricted prepaid matcher for bounded sessions while preserving the legacy unbounded entrypoint; an exhausted partial walk cannot report complete/Idle.
boundaries.ownership: A session owns the prepaid index and ledger until teardown; both admission counters advance together or neither does.
limits: This is retained index accounting, not an RSS, arbitrary filesystem-call duration, allocator-overhead or total-runtime bound.
The actual NativeSearchBackend trait adapter and separately installed native worker are absent at this immutable checkpoint.
dependencies: vendored Nucleo prepaid index and UTF-32 planning

boundaries.origin: Stage A custom retained owner around the original native search implementation
intentional_changes: Expose separate operation and cleanup outcomes for bounded startup, lease close and owner shutdown; preserve legacy anyhow entrypoints.
Refund capacity only on Joined cleanup, retaining operation failure; quarantine capacity on unconfirmed cleanup.
Keep accepted startup and close jobs alive after observer cancellation; retain the first native failure independently if later reporter teardown panics.
boundaries.ownership: Preparing, ready and closing entries remain with the retained owner. An error alone is not a joined-cleanup receipt.
limits: Existing FileSearchStartError compatibility is conservative; legacy flattened errors do not become new proof of cleanup.
Runtime destruction, process abort and arbitrary stuck native work remain outside successful-join guarantees.

origin.mapping: Foreign original paths drop the codex-rs/third-party/nucleo/ prefix. These files were vendored after the OpenAI import; import_blob is absent.

intentional_changes: Add fallible prepaid single-column arena, candidate/snapshot/in-flight arrays, matcher scratch and typed capacity failure while retaining ordinary constructors.
Preflight borrowed UTF-32 payload charge and allocate exact backing storage preserving ASCII/CRLF, Unicode and grapheme conversion behavior.
Retain the earlier safely demonstrated matrix-extent correction and documented mechanical lint edits; do not count these foreign patches as native subsystem extraction.
boundaries.ownership: Bounded index construction owns prepaid buffers; the enclosing native supervisor must still stop producers and join actual OS workers after index shutdown.
limits: Accounting depends on pinned Rust allocator/Arc layout and Rayon indexed-collection behavior; upstream/toolchain changes require re-audit.
Fallible selected allocation paths do not guarantee recovery from every system OOM or process-aborting failure.

boundaries.origin: Custom persistent component transport, not an imported native subsystem
intentional_changes: Return response observer plus reserved cleanup immediately after paired admission; cancellation before acquiring both lanes sends no partial request, and dropped observers never replay accepted work.
Preserve full request-before-cleanup ordering and return opaque successful cleanup JSON so callers validate domain receipts; retain call_with_cleanup/release compatibility.
Add opt-in serialized logical JSON body limits before admission or spooling/deserialization; keep existing headers and wire format.
Keep ordinary default storage bodies unbounded and fixed 64 KiB control allowance; reject configured reply caps below 64 KiB instead of silently clamping.

Carry typed local payload overflow through terminal observations; local rejection keeps healthy cleanup lanes, whereas oversized peer payload terminates transport with unconfirmed domain cleanup. Never infer typed remote errors from legacy strings.
boundaries.ownership: Existing session owners retain accepted operations; reserved control capacity survives ordinary saturation. A transport response is distinct from native join/durability.
limits: Transport opt-in bounds do not validate search identities, results or domain cleanup; the search adapter must do that.
Session default behavior and storage wire compatibility are intentionally preserved.

boundaries.origin: Existing custom catalog and retained persistent-process startup
intentional_changes: Allow explicit existing absolute startup cwd in the retained startup task, rejecting relative cwd/entrypoint or invalid directories before spawning. Apply child current_dir once without host/per-lease chdir.
Keep canonical package entrypoint, package identity and state binding; existing connect/connect_with_limits still start in package_dir and one-shot/stream defaults are unchanged.
Admit file_search contract 1 packages in catalog, reject incompatible selected upgrades, and reject one-shot manager Call for the persistent provider/lease lifecycle.
boundaries.ownership: Launch options are fixed for a process lifetime; package discovery and compatibility stay with the catalog. No filesystem authority is added to the contract.
limits: A startup cwd is not a sandbox and does not normalize original search roots.
Catalog admission and fixture upgrade checks do not establish a packaged native worker or production search selection.

boundaries.origin: New provider/lease wire service built on already accepted neutral search contracts
intentional_changes: Define file_search/default contract 1 initialization, open, query update, snapshot poll, release and provider shutdown, with provider/lease/epoch identities and typed operation versus cleanup outcomes.
Preserve decimal u64 identity bits and same-platform non-UTF8 paths; reject invalid paths, bounds, indices, counts and impossible Idle/completion frames.
Synchronously reserve Preparing work before spawning handlers so release can find startup; retain abandoned poll/update ownership and bounded retired receipts.

Refund quotas after Joined close even on operation failure; quarantine unconfirmed cleanup and fence the provider. Oversized encoded snapshots return ResourceExhausted with owned cleanup instead of truncated success.
Offer a generic persistent stdio runner and factory context with explicit base/config/state/limits, independent of Core and any concrete native matcher.
boundaries.ownership: SearchService retains factory initialization, lease work and shutdown; the stdio runner drains accepted service work and response handlers before transport finish.
limits: Service tests use controlled backends; the runner is not itself a packaged native search plugin.
The immutable SDK plan contains historical proposal/status text; typed source and separately recorded evidence are authoritative for implemented names and test status.

boundaries.origin: New implementation of the previously accepted neutral SearchBackend surface
intentional_changes: Connect one selected process in explicit immutable cwd with negotiated payload/resource ceilings; no reconnect/replay or fallback to another implementation on failure.
Serialize epoch allocation plus bounded admission without waiting for an earlier open response. Retain paired cleanup through abandoned startup and validate release_reply domain receipts.
Check roots/options/query limits before encoding/admission, validate identities/methods before accepting replies, and fence stale or mismatched responses.
Retain accepted operations after observer cancellation; final public backend/session drop requests owned cleanup. Preserve original operation failure when release is uncertain.
boundaries.ownership: Provider and lease owner tasks retain transport and cleanup independently of public observers; reserved resource capacity is released only under explicit cleanup receipts.
limits: Real independent peer-process tests validate transport/lifecycle behavior but peers are protocol fixtures, not the native matcher.
No installed native worker, App Server/TUI backend composition or real GUI search replacement is present at this checkpoint.
The post-test missing-identity error branch in process_open was compiled by scoped lint but was not separately exercised in the recorded 22-case run.

boundaries.origin: Existing OpenAI in-process App Server client plus earlier custom low-level storage drain

symbols.anchor: pub fn shutdown(self) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = IoResult<()>> + Send

intentional_changes: Replace separate 45-second acknowledgement/join waits and unbounded command send with one admission/acknowledgement/join deadline derived from the existing 200-second embedded budget plus 5 seconds.

Capture the owning runtime and start retained coordination synchronously when shutdown is requested; an unpolled/cancelled receipt or enum wrapper no longer drops unobserved worker ownership. Future construction outside an entered runtime is preserved.
Retain first operation failure while still observing worker completion; surface acknowledgement loss, worker panic and forced deadline as errors with explicit cleanup uncertainty.
On deadline request abort, return uncertainty within the public deadline, and retain the worker for eventual join; do not claim lower-level storage cleanup from a facade abort.
Expose/name the shared low-level budget only; its 200-second value and unrelated low-level implementation are unchanged in this delta. Remote client shutdown remains separate.
boundaries.ownership: The coordinator owns the facade worker through join or abort-and-join fallback. A live cooperative runtime is required for retained cleanup to progress.
limits: This repairs an existing coupled client; no separately installable App Server/session orchestration component is introduced.
The immutable checkpoint has the old lag-test fixture that drops its command receiver; the first executable client gate reports 39/40, including all 12 new shutdown cases passing.
The corrected 40/40 client gate is a later fixture revision outside bb03; it must not be attributed to this immutable tree.
